releases.name: GHVST Capture
releases.headline: The Film Desk: the phone now makes real, watchable videos - with music, with the screen off
fixed: Pictures the app itself took now count as film material. Before this, a phone holding a hundred screenshots built a film out of nothing and reported 'no pictures found'.

Film and Studio both dropped every frame before the last one: the muxer only started while draining the end of the stream, so the MP4 opened, had a size, and played as nothing. One shared encoder path now starts the muxer the moment the format is known, and the file is only called finished when it holds real frames.
A film can carry music. Any MP3/M4A/WAV/AAC/OGG/FLAC is decoded, laid under the picture at bed level, and muxed as a real AAC track.
Every finished film is published to the gallery and shares through a content:// URI, because a file:// path is refused by Android 7 and up.
Film jobs survive the screen going off and the phone restarting: a queued job is picked up again after boot.
The agent can drive the whole thing: MAKE VIDEO, ADD MUSIC, PROOF, JOBS, CANCEL, SOUNDS, FORGE.
New FILM DESK screen: picture count, seconds per picture, music picker, the live queue with cancel, and a proof panel for every finished film.
proof: A 1080x1920 H.264 film, 24 fps, 288 frames, 12.000 s, 1,796,690 bytes - read back off the device and verified with ffprobe.
A film with music: H.264 video plus AAC 44.1 kHz audio, 8.057 s, 518,871 bytes.
Both films were made while the phone's screen was off and the keyguard was up - the overnight case.
The SHA-256 in the app's own proof panel matched the pulled file byte for byte.
